capitals.name: Khachen (Haterk)
capitals.note: The Kingdom page lists Khachen, Haterk and Vaykunik as capitals, the Principality page Gandzasar, Haterk and Tsar; no years or coordinates are given, so one seat in the Khachen valley (approximate) stands for the whole span.

rulers.name: Hasan-Jalal Dola
rulers.title: prince of Khachen, last king of Artsakh
rulers.note: Assassinated in 1261 by the Ilkhanid ruler Arghun; the page lists no earlier rulers with years.

correction.text: Artsakh and Khachen: 'Syunik and Artsakh provinces', Gardman and Mazaz of Utik and Varazhnunik of Ayrarat; from the 16th century five Artsakh melikdoms and the Kashatagh melikdom of Syunik

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1000-1603. The Kingdom of Artsakh page names the provinces and cantons but no boundary or area; the Karabakh region (54 grid cells, about 13,700 km2 on the gazetteer) is the reading, which leaves out Gardman, Varazhnunik and the Syunik side. The Principality page adds that Khachen 'dominated the region' from the 12th century and gives the Khamsa from 1603; the shape is not narrowed for 1261-1603 because the pages give no change of land.

ledger.note: c. 1000: the Kingdom of Artsakh (Khachen) appears. Infobox 'Established: 1000', a vassal of the Armenian kingdom around 1000; 'Contemporary sources referred to it as the Khachen.'

1214: the house of Hasan-Jalal begins to rule Khachen and Artsakh. 'Began ruling much of Khachen and Artsakh in 1214'; they founded Gandzasar monastery in 1216. Under Hasan-Jalal (1214-1261) Artsakh accepted Georgian, then Mongol, suzerainty (early 13th century, Kingdom of Artsakh page).

1261: Dizak and Gardman join Khachen. The infobox lists 'Acquisition of Dizak and Gardman: 1261'; the page names no counterpart and no detail, so the lost party is 'nobody' and the region is a reading (Dizak read as Khojavend rayon; Gardman, in Utik, is not drawn).

1261: Hasan-Jalal is assassinated and the kingdom becomes the principality of Khachen. 'Assassination of Hasan Jalal, last king of Artsakh: 1261'; he 'was assassinated by the Ilkhanid ruler Arghun', after which the rulers lost the royal title and 'continued as a principality over Syunik'; the Principality page dates 'Established: 1261'.

1603: Persia puts the Khamsa under a protectorate. 'In 1603 the Persians established a protectorate over the Khamsa'; the Principality of Khachen (infobox 1261-1603) gives way to the five Melikdoms of Karabakh.

wars.name: Ilkhanid killing of Hasan-Jalal
wars.outcome: Hasan-Jalal Dola, last king of Artsakh, was assassinated by the Ilkhanid ruler Arghun in 1261 and the rulers lost the royal title.
wars.note: Early 13th-century Georgian and then Mongol suzerainty is undated on the page; the Georgia and Ilkhanate dossiers carry any vassal tint.

wars.name: Persian protectorate over the Khamsa
wars.outcome: The Persians established a protectorate over the Khamsa in 1603; the melikdoms kept Armenian autonomy through the Persian-Ottoman wars.

certainty.note: Mountain principality: no page gives a boundary; the Karabakh region is a soft reading.

sources.title: Kingdom of Artsakh
sources.note: Established 1000, territory, Hasan-Jalal 1214-1261, 1261 end of royal title.

notes: No Cliopatria row for Artsakh/Khachen before the Republic of Artsakh. One dossier for the Kingdom of Artsakh (1000-1261) and the Principality of Khachen (1261-1603), a rename in 1261 (rule 2); the successors, the Melikdoms of Karabakh (Khamsa, 1603 to the early 19th century), need a dossier (suggested slug melikdoms-of-karabakh; the khanates-of-the-caucasus dossier of eu-19-f may cover the Karabakh Khanate). The bagratid-armenia dossier lists a Bagratid successor 'Kingdom of Artsakh (Khachen)' and carries no year-level relation; the Syunik side (Kingdom of Syunik) overlaps in the 12th century on the pages ('continued as a principality over Syunik'). The page's founding sentence (a cadet branch of the Syunid dynasty named after Khachen) is not dated; 1000 is the infobox year; 1182 'subdivision of the kingdom' is in the infobox without detail. Capital coordinates are approximate. wikidata null.
